question.prompt: How many ordered triples of integers \((a,b,c)\) satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} |a+b|+c&=19,\\ ab+|c|&=97? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.explanation:
Changing both \(a\) and \(b\) to their negatives preserves \(|a+b|\) and \(ab\). We can therefore first solve the equations when \(s=a+b\ge0\), then obtain negative sums by reversing both signs.

The first equation gives \(c=19-s\). Split according to the sign of \(c\) so that the second absolute value can also be removed.

If \(c\ge0\), then \(0\le s\le19\), and the second equation becomes
\[
ab+19-a-b=97.
\]
Adding 1 after rearranging makes the left side a product:
\[
(a-1)(b-1)=79.
\]
Since 79 is prime, the integer factor pairs are \((1,79)\), \((79,1)\), \((-1,-79)\), and \((-79,-1)\). These give \(a+b=82\) or \(-78\), neither in \([0,19]\). Thus this case has no solutions, including none with \(a+b=0\).

If \(c<0\), then \(s>19\) and \(|c|=s-19\). Hence
\[
ab+a+b-19=97,
\qquad (a+1)(b+1)=117.
\]
The factors cannot both be negative, because that would give \(a+b<0\). Since \(117=3^2\cdot13\), its positive unordered factor pairs are exactly
\[
(1,117),\quad(3,39),\quad(9,13).
\]
Subtracting 1 from each factor gives the unordered pairs
\[
(a,b)=(0,116),\quad(2,38),\quad(8,12).
\]
Their sums are 116, 40, and 20, all greater than 19, and their respective values of \(c=19-s\) are \(-97,-21,-1\). Thus every listed pair satisfies its case conditions and both original equations.

Each pair has two distinct orders. Reversing both signs gives two further triples with negative sum, disjoint from those already counted. The factor lists exhaust both cases, and there are no zero-sum solutions to count separately. Therefore the total is
\[
3\cdot2\cdot2=\boxed{12},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Remove the absolute values and find factor pairs
